question: For male legislators from Louisiana, how many distinct legislators were actively serving on December 31 of each year from more than 30 years since their first term up to less than 50 years, grouping the results by the exact number of years elapsed since their first term?
sql:
-- Let me also verify the full result one more time to make sure it's complete
WITH male_la_legislators AS (
    SELECT l.id_bioguide, l.first_name, l.last_name
    FROM legislators l
    WHERE l.gender = 'M' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms lt WHERE lt.id_bioguide = l.id_bioguide AND lt.state = 'LA'
    )
),
first_terms AS (
    SELECT ml.id_bioguide, MIN(lt.term_start) as first_term_start
    FROM male_la_legislators ml
    JOIN legislators_terms lt ON ml.id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide
    GROUP BY ml.id_bioguide
),
year_range AS (
    SELECT UNNEST(generate_series(1811, 2020)) AS year_num
),
dec31_check AS (
    SELECT 
        ft.id_bioguide,
        ft.first_term_start,
        yr.year_num,
        CAST(CONCAT(yr.year_num, '-12-31') AS DATE) AS dec31_date,
        lt.term_start,
        lt.term_end,
        CASE 
            WHEN CAST(lt.term_start AS DATE) <= CAST(CONCAT(yr.year_num, '-12-31') AS DATE) 
             AND CAST(lt.term_end AS DATE) >= CAST(CONCAT(yr.year_num, '-12-31') AS DATE)
            THEN 1 ELSE 0
        END AS is_active
    FROM first_terms ft
    CROSS JOIN year_range yr
    JOIN legislators_terms lt ON ft.id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide
    WHERE yr.year_num BETWEEN CAST(YEAR(CAST(lt.term_start AS DATE)) AS INTEGER) 
                          AND CAST(YEAR(CAST(lt.term_end AS DATE)) AS INTEGER) + 1
),
active_years AS (
    SELECT 
        dc.id_bioguide,
        dc.first_term_start,
        dc.year_num,
        dc.dec31_date,
        date_diff('year', CAST(dc.first_term_start AS DATE), dc.dec31_date) AS years_elapsed
    FROM dec31_check dc
    WHERE dc.is_active = 1
)
SELECT years_elapsed, COUNT(DISTINCT id_bioguide) AS distinct_legislators
FROM active_years
WHERE years_elapsed > 30 AND years_elapsed < 50
GROUP BY years_elapsed
ORDER BY years_elapsed

-- The Dec 31 dates that could fall within this term range from year(term_start) to year(term_end)
-- For each such year Y, the Dec 31 is 'Y-12-31'
-- It falls within the term if: CAST(term_start AS DATE) <= 'Y-12-31' AND CAST(term_end AS DATE) >= 'Y-12-31'

-- Let me generate a numbers table to create years
WITH male_la_legislators AS (
    SELECT l.id_bioguide, l.first_name, l.last_name
    FROM legislators l
    WHERE l.gender = 'M' AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM legislators_terms lt WHERE lt.id_bioguide = l.id_bioguide AND lt.state = 'LA'
    )
),
first_terms AS (
    SELECT ml.id_bioguide, MIN(lt.term_start) as first_term_start
    FROM male_la_legislators ml
    JOIN legislators_terms lt ON ml.id_bioguide = lt.id_bioguide
    GROUP BY ml.id_bioguide
),
-- Get all unique years we might need (from earliest possible to latest possible)
year_range AS (
    SELECT UNNEST(generate_series(1811, 2020)) AS year_num
),
-- For each legislator-term-year combination, check if Dec 31 falls within the term

    SELECT 
        ft.id_bioguide,
        ft.first_term_start,
        yr.year_num,
        CAST(CONCAT(yr.year_num, '-12-31') AS DATE) AS dec31_date,
        lt.term_start,
        lt.term_end,
        CASE 
            WHEN CAST(lt.term_start AS DATE) <= CAST(CONCAT(yr.year_num, '-12-31') AS DATE) 
             AND CAST(lt.term_end AS DATE) >= CAST(CONCAT(yr.year_num, '-12-31') AS DATE)
